task:
Listen up, <Ranger>! You should already know that we, the Pelengs, can decide on our sex and change it whenever we wish. Don't you know that? Sure we do! We need no surgery to change our sex unlike some retarded races. All we need to do is get authorisation from the Sacred Lyakushery - it is our race's ancient tradition. For the Pelengs, unauthorised change if sex is the second severest crime after whistling. Candidates for the change of sex have to go through a sacred ritual. Previously they put on masks of the sacred animals - pachvarashes, and fought with each other. But presently, as new technologies evolved, the ritual became more cultured and civilised. Thousands of Pelengs wish to pass it every year... 

But let's get down to business! Our honoured mistress President decided to change her sex. However, in order to get an authorisation from the Sacred Lyakushery one has to go to planet <ToPlanet> in the system of <ToStar>, but she is extremely busy and just can not leave planet <FromPlanet>. So, if you can get there before <Date> and pass the ritual instead of the mistress President, we will pay you <Money> cr. Don't worry that you're not a Peleng. Our custom is that one does not have to be present at the sex selection ritual, but can send someone else instead, even if it's not a Peleng.
success:
Excellent, <Ranger>! A courier from planet <ToPlanet> has already brought the change of sex authorisation. You should have seen his mug!!! You're the first one ever to obtain such authorisation for the last ten years! 

Accept <Money> cr as a personal gift from our honoured mister President.
loc.1.0:
You landed in a common Peleng spaceport. But once you had prepared yourself for several traditionally tiresome hours of Peleng customs procedures (what do they look for every time? There is nothing forbidden anyway!), a Peleng in a long green cloak approached you. 

- I believe you are <Ranger>? You arrived to obtain an authorisation for the change of sex for a powerful Peleng, didn't you? I was assigned to welcome you and show you to the Temple. I am going to take you to the Chief Distributor, who will tell you about the <clr>ritual<clrEnd>.

He waived to the customs officers and they passed you without any checks! Looks like participants to the ritual are in high esteem among the Pelengs. You got into a gravicar and in a half hour arrived to the Temple, which, amazingly, was like an ordinary administrative building. Moments later you found yourself in an office of another Peleng who introduced himself as Chief Distributor lyakusha Buor O'Cratt. Probably you should say something.
loc.1.1: - Should I also send you on a secret mission? - laughed Buor O'Cratt in return. He definitely has an extensive experience of accepting rangers in his office!
loc.1.2:
- Thanks to modern technologies you will be turned into a <clr>pachvarash<clrEnd>. It is a little sacred creature with three legs and six eyes. Then you will be put into a pachvarash village where you will have to justify that you are worthy of an authorisation for the change of sex. Thus you will need to accomplish either of these: 

1. Gain more weight - up to <clr>100 hg<clrEnd> (just eat as much as you can), dig a burrow at least <clr>50 ar<clrEnd> deep and win respect among other pachvarashes by at least <clr>50%<clrEnd> (to increase your respect level, fight with other pachvarashes).

2. Beat the pachvarash Chief. Bear in mind however, that in order to be eligible for a fight with the Chief, you'll have to bring <clr>5 scalps<clrEnd> of pachvarashes killed by you. 

It's not that hard, is it?
loc.1.3: - There is no time in the pachvarash village, - said the lyakusha. - Just do everything right!
loc.57.0:
You made it! Weight of [p4] hg, a burrow [p3] ar deep and [p2]% of respect - it is more than enough to win! The lights died and the pachvarash village has vanished...

You find yourself in an armchair, in your regular body. And it seems like you can even talk again!!! There is no druid behind you anymore but in front of you dazed lyakusha Buor O'Cratt stood smiling.

- This is unbelievable, <Ranger>! - he mumbled. - You can hardly imagine how unbelievable it is!

With a glance at a calendar-watch behind the Peleng, you were amazed to find out it was still <CurDate>, and only a couple of hours had passed since your last conversation. It feels like you had lived an entire life! Alright, now it's time to say everything you want to this Peleng!
loc.57.1:
You have beaten the Chief himself! Now you are the main pachvarash in the village. You will become a new Chief and other pachvarashes will bring you best food and dig your burrow. How beautiful your life is going to be! But what's going on? Why is it getting dark so quickly? What's wrong with you? Why is the pachvarash village vanishing?!..

You find yourself in an armchair, in your regular body. And it seems like you can even talk again!!! There is no druid behind you anymore but in front of you dazed lyakusha Buor O'Cratt stood smiling.

- This is unbelievable, <Ranger>! - he mumbled. - You can hardly imagine how unbelievable it is!

With a glance at a calendar-watch behind the Peleng, you were amazed to find out it was still <CurDate>, and only a couple of hours had passed since your last conversation. It feels like you had lived an entire life! Alright, now it's time to say everything you want to this Peleng!
loc.58.0:
- As far as I know, on planet <FromPlanet> they said that thousands of Pelengs <clr>wish<clrEnd> to pass the ritual every year. I'd rather say that millions want to do that, but none of them dares - they are all afraid! 

- Then why are all those rituals for? Why not just prohibiting change of sex instead? 

- Nothing should be prohibited! Any prohibition is foreign to the Pelengs - lovers of liberty! As to proving oneself worthy - they are all for it. That's why we introduced the ritual. The result is the same - no Peleng has passed the pachvarash village since it was created {300} years ago!
loc.59.0:
- Given that a Peleng law or tradition is hardly to survive for more than 100 years, the change of sex authorisation ritual is indeed our most ancient tradition!

- Then what about the tale of Pelengs taking pachvarash masks on and fighting each other in the past?

- Yes, that's what we did in the beginning. A thousand of candidates in pachvarash masks fought to death until only one remained and received the precious authorisation. But after we stole the virtual reality technology from the Humans, the procedure became more cultured and civilised. Indeed, why giving an authorisation to even a single candidate when you can kill them all?
loc.60.0:
- Because you are not Peleng! Your psychology is different and enabled you to avoid our nice traps. For instance, it never occurred to you to swim in a beautiful swamp near the village after digging a burrow or a fight - about 40% of Peleng candidates drowned there. Or take for example the tsianutick bush over there on the hill - oh so many Pelengs tried to extract its root to make a poison and kill the Chief! All of them died in paws of a helldas that dwells on the hill. You did not even notice the bush... And the burrow?! Tell me, what kind of a retard can dig a burrow at an angle? Didn't you notice it was crumbling all the time? Any sane Peleng digs straight down - and at the depth of {49} ar arrives at a specially arranged lake of boiling lava... Never mind, soon we age going to steal from <clr>MacroHard<clrEnd> company a universal patch, which automatically adjusts any program's engine according to its user's race, and this backdoor for getting an authorisation will be closed!

You returned to the spaceport in a rather jolly mood - it's great to be something but Peleng! The most delightful is that on planet <FromPlanet> a truly deserved prize of <Money> cr awaits you.
loc.61.0: After saying goodbye to the Peleng, you returned to the spaceport. Despite the success of the mission, your mood is rather bad. Only the anticipation of the prize of <Money> cr on planet <FromPlanet> somewhat comforted you.
loc.63.0:
"I'd live to spend my whole life in this burrow! - you thought. - Wait, I already begin to think like an animal, I am a highly intelligent creature!!!" 

It's time to move on.
loc.63.1:
The pachvarashes stayed in their burrows and did nothing. It seems as if they are afraid to do anything themselves.

Determination is your second name! It is time for the next step. What do you do now?
loc.63.2:
This night on planet <ToPlanet> - is the best of all nights. The sky is full of stars and it's pleasant to remember that some time ago you run around pirate systems at a wheel of the spaceship.

Your burrow is well located - the view of the sky is magnificent! Well, at least you are lucky in something. Let's go on.
loc.63.3:
It would be nice to have a deal with another pachvarash; together we can complete the ritual faster. An ability to speak - that's what makes a humanoid different from an animal! But don't mind, as soon as you get though it, you'll be able to speak it all out!

What to do now?
loc.63.4: Don't stop at what has been accomplished! You will not pass the ritual by sitting in your burrow. It's time to act!
loc.63.5: It is safe to stay in the burrow. But you should not just stay there, you have to act. A wind started and small particles of soil are blown around like snow. You don't feel like going outside, but you have to! Or is it better to dig some more inside?
loc.63.6: You have carefully spelled your name with a toe in the dust by your door: "<Ranger>". You can not speak, but nobody can take the right to write! "Long live free media!" you thought. And it does not even matter that the wind or other pachvarashes will erase the inscription in a matter of minutes - you have announced your protest to the whole world! Maybe it's time to do something useful?
loc.63.7: Everything has changed in your burrow - it's damp and dirty, and no one to talk to. And nothing to speak with... What boredom! Maybe you should have something to eat or beat somebody up?
loc.63.8:
You looked around your burrow. What an ugly place! Will you really have to live here and dig it further?! You tried to curse, but all you managed were some shrieks and howling. Here we go, it turned out that you can not speak anymore!!! 

You looked outside. Other pachvarashes minded their own business - some ate grass, some fought, some stayed in their burrows. Maybe you should also do something?
loc.63.9:
A stone plate, installed nearby your burrow, contained the following inscription:

-------------------
TWO WAYS TO WIN:

1. PEACEFUL:
- Gain more weight - up to <clr>100 hg<clrEnd>
- Dig a burrow <clr>50 ar<clrEnd> deep
- Achieve respect among pachvarashes of at least <clr>50%<clrEnd>

2. OFFENSIVE:
- Beat the Chief (get <clr>5<clrEnd> scalps first) 
-------------------

You returned to the burrow. What do you do next?

loc.66.0: You can eat some tarnished grass around your burrow - it's not extremely nutritious, but rather safe. On the other hand you can go to a nice meadow in the centre of the village, where you may have a clash with other pachvarashes. Are you going there?

jump.200.text: Well, I'm really glad! Now excuse me - I have to go to the spaceport...
jump.201.text: How come?! They told me thousands of Pelengs pass this ritual every year!!!
jump.202.text: 300 years only?! But they say it is the oldest Peleng tradition!
jump.203.text: Then I am cooler than the Pelengs! Now excuse me, have to go to the spaceport...

jump.207.text: Turn me into a pachvarash??? No way, that was not in the deal, I go back to the spaceport!!!
jump.210.desc:
- Good! We begin your transformation into a pachvarash! - Peleng said, pushing a button on the wall. 

A small droid rolled to you from the far end of the room. It moved around you as if assessing a target. Then it stopped behind. A cold metal of the robot's metal connectors touched your back and eyes. "Connection established, - said an electronic voice of the robot. - Counting down: three... two... one..." Your knees began to tremble, it was scary. Your conscience faded, and it became dark... 

Finally you realised you could see. You found yourself in a cave. This looks like your burrow. You examined yourself and found out you had three legs! And the whole body was covered in fur. By the way, you had six eyes! And what's that strange bump on the back of your head? Isn't that the ultrasonic locator-sensor?! It is!!! You immediately tried it to determine your condition: weight [p4] hg, health [p1]%, burrow depth [p3] ar. This locator also enables you to scan the neighbourhood! So, the village, rather big one, is surrounded by three swamps, and from the fourth side it has a hill, where some bushes grow. Both the swamps and the hill are most likely impenetrable. Then it is impossible to run away from here, you will have to play by local rules. By the way, how many other pachvarashes are there? You started counting: "ten... twenty... thirty... hundred", damn it, you stumbled! Alright, there are many of them, can't be counted. But you could measure their respect for you: [p2]%.

param.0.crit:
Your strength gave out. You are not worthy of an authorisation to change sex. What is the reason to stay alive then? I mean, you probably can find a reason, but other pachvarashes did not see any...

You failed the test! To die a pachvarash - what can be worse?
param.1.crit: Your behaviour at the village was extremely antisocial and respect for you fell flat. You felt it when a crowd of furious pachvarashes surrounded your burrow and threw stones in it. What can be worse for a self-respectable pachvarash, especially for an ex-space ranger, than to be buried in its own burrow...
param.2.crit: You burrow has almost crumbled! "Not a big deal, I can bum it over somewhere" you thought, but other pachvarashes' opinion was different. Once a threatening crowd of several dozens of pachvarashes gathered around you, you realised, bums are not respected here. Your nerves snapped there and with a wild shriek you darted out. The crowd ran for you, they followed before you left the village and drowned in the nearby swamp. What a horrible, silly death!
param.3.crit: Just look at yourself with your own six eyes!!! There's almost nothing to see! You're so skinny you can hide behind a fishing rod! You should have eaten more. You lost conscience due to permanent hunger and death followed soon...
param.4.crit: Пачварашей стало гораздо больше, чем нор, где им можно было жить. Несколько тварей рванили в вашу нору. Они набросились на вас и растерзали в клочья. Вы не справились с заданием и у мерли в теле животного - это настоящий позор для пеленга!
